thread:
sam: quick design q 1200px dashboard tile. capacity controls look cramped. current layout: min/max steppers, burst toggle, pool picker, SLO slider, cost badge. thinking of a vertical compact variant for small tiles (stack min/max above burst + pool) so elements breathe. thoughts?
maya: vertical makes sense for very narrow tiles, but we should avoid increasing tab stops. maybe a responsive layout: horizontal at >=1280, vertical under 900. also show a tiny predicted cost delta when users tweak min/max (like +$0.05/hr).
zain: engineering: predicted cost calc is doable but needs backend rate limits. we can show a client-side estimate using token-rate heuristics for the prototype. accessibility: make sure predicted cost text is aria-live when it changes.
ellie: UX: guardrails for SLO slider are important. propose placing soft/hard guard labels on the slider track and a tooltip that explains what each guard means. also advocate an A/B test for default state (expanded vs collapsed) to measure feature discovery.
niko: dev note: keyboard order should follow visual order. prefer DOM order: min -> max -> pool -> burst -> slo -> cost. if vertical, combine min/max into one composite control with internal tabbing to reduce outer tab stops. for popovers use role="dialog" and focus trap.
maya: copy nits: replace "Burst" with "Temporary burst capacity" in long layouts, but use "Burst" on tiny chips. cost delta should be short, like "+$0.05/hr". l10n: keep under 45 chars.
sam: action items: zain will prototype client-side cost delta and aria-live; ellie to mock vertical responsive + guardrail labels; niko to list focus-trap complexity and estimate; maya to write final copy variants.
